set.layering_notes: San Joaquin County has no county housing trust fund, no county housing bond and no inclusionary ordinance; the County's own capital for multifamily is limited to HUD pass-through funds administered by the Human Services Agency Neighborhood Preservation Division (sjchsa.org), while the regional gap lender is the SJCOG-sponsored San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund and the main voucher and development partner is the Housing Authority of the County of San Joaquin (HACSJ). Classified as grant because the BHSA Integrated Plan funds housing capital (two capital development projects, the Tiny Homes project and Edison House, BHSA share at or below $450,000 per unit) and project-based rental and operating subsidies for housing. BHSA is the County's largest discretionary housing stream and the realistic source of project-based operating subsidy for PSH units in the unincorporated county and Stockton; capital is limited to the two named projects, so new deals should pitch rental or operating subsidies for behavioral health set-aside units rather than construction money. Behavioral Health Services also carries Homekey+ (Bridge to Home, $15,900,896 agreement with CVLIHC approved January 13, 2026) and Behavioral Health Bridge Housing Round 3 contracts, and is building the SJ BeWell campus with a $38.2 million BHCIP Round 2 award (March 2026). Pre-qualification through the BHS RFQ is the entry point for developers. The Board file (source) links the board order, the 490-page DHCS Integrated Plan submission (FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=45761) and the June 2, 2026 presentation.

reason: Integrated Plan funds capital development and housing rental and operating subsidies, so funding_type is grant; board order confirms $295,750,706 approved June 2, 2026 by a 5-0 vote.
